prompt: A line has equation $y = 3$. What is $y$ on this line when $x = 100$?
hint: Look closely at the equation. There is no $x$ in it at all, so what can $x$ change?

hints.text: Look closely at the equation. There is no $x$ in it at all, so what can $x$ change?
Think of $y = 3$ as $y = 0x + 3$. Putting in $x = 100$ gives $0 \times 100 + 3$, and zero times any number is zero.
The value of $y$ is always $3$ on this line, so $y = 3$ when $x = 100$.

explanation: The equation $y = 3$ can be written as $y = 0x + 3$, a line with slope $0$.
A slope of zero means the line never rises or falls, so it is horizontal and every point has the same height.
At $x = 100$, or at any other $x$, the value of $y$ is $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A flat hallway
steps: Start at height $3$ and move with slope $0$: every step across stays at height $3$.
Walk $100$ steps and you are still at height $3$.
